glossary.definition: The unit models read and bill by; roughly three quarters of an English word on average.
Small language model: cheaper and faster, good for simple, well-defined tasks.
Trying a cheap model first and escalating to a stronger one only when a check fails.
Share of input tokens served from the prompt cache instead of processed fresh.
The point up to which a prompt is cached; everything before it must be identical.
Time to live: how long a cached item stays available before it expires.
The cap on how many tokens a model may generate in one response.
The maximum number of iterations or tool calls an agent may take for one task.
The maximum number of tokens a model can consider in one request.
Retrying after increasing delays (1 s, 2 s, 4 s…) to avoid overloading a service.
An asynchronous API that processes many requests at a discount within a delivery window, often 24 hours.
Reserved model capacity paid for by time rather than per token.
A store of full answers keyed by the embedding of the question, so a new question similar enough to a cached one gets the stored answer without a model call.
A semantic-cache match that returns a stored answer to a question it does not fit, such as a UAE roaming answer for a USA roaming question.
One minus cosine similarity; a distance threshold of 0.10 is the same as requiring similarity of at least 0.90.
Removing or retiring cached entries when the content they were built from changes, instead of waiting for them to expire.
Splitting spend by tags such as team, feature, customer and run.
Spend per business outcome, such as ₹ per invoice or per resolved ticket.
A limit on tokens, rupees or steps for a single agent run.

symptomRouter.symptom: Most requests are simple, but everything runs on the top model
symptomRouter.advice: Route easy traffic to a small model and escalate only when checks fail.

symptomRouter.symptom: Every call resends the same long system prompt and tool list
symptomRouter.advice: Put the stable prefix first so the provider bills it at the cached rate.

symptomRouter.symptom: Agent loops run long and outputs are wordy
symptomRouter.advice: Cap output, set a step budget, and trim tools and tool results.

symptomRouter.symptom: Long conversations get slower and pricier every turn
symptomRouter.advice: Summarize old turns and clear used tool output once context crosses a threshold.

symptomRouter.symptom: Traffic spikes force us to pay for peak capacity
symptomRouter.advice: Queue background work, shift it off-peak, and set quotas per tenant.

symptomRouter.symptom: We process large datasets that nobody waits on
symptomRouter.advice: Submit them through a batch API at about half the price.

symptomRouter.symptom: Thousands of users ask the same FAQ in different words and each one pays for a fresh LLM answer
symptomRouter.advice: Put a semantic cache in front of the model for FAQ intents only, tune the threshold on near-miss pairs, and purge entries when the source changes.

symptomRouter.symptom: Nobody knows which feature or customer drives the LLM bill, or an agent loop ran up a large charge
symptomRouter.advice: Tag every call at a gateway, report unit costs, and add per-run budgets, per-customer caps and anomaly alerts.
